cards.text: Job just asked his friends why the wicked live on, growing old and increasing in power (Job 21:7). Now Eliphaz the Temanite, one of Job's three friends (Job 2:11), answers him. He opens with questions, and friend, when a friend opens with QUESTIONS, you buckle up: “Can a man be of use to God? Can even a wise man benefit Him?”

cards.question: Eliphaz asks Job, “Does it delight the Almighty that you are righteous?” Then he asks if God profits when Job's ways are blameless. True or false: Eliphaz is saying God profits from Job's goodness.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz asks, “Is it for your reverence that He rebukes you and enters into judgment against you?” Translation, friend: in Eliphaz's eyes, Job's reverence is NOT why God is taking him to court.

cards.question: So Eliphaz rules out Job's reverence as the reason for his trouble. What does Eliphaz say the reason is instead?

cards.text: Now Eliphaz stops asking and starts LISTING: he says Job needlessly demanded security from his brothers and took the clothing of the naked. Friend, this list is like one of those store receipts that rolls out longer than your ARM.

cards.question: Next on Eliphaz's list are the weary and the famished. What does he claim Job did to them?

answers.text: Charged them for water and food
Sent them away to another town

cards.text: Eliphaz adds that all this happened “while the land belonged to a mighty man, and a man of honor lived on it.”

cards.question: Eliphaz's list of people he says Job wronged keeps going. He says Job sent ___ away empty-handed, and the strength of the fatherless was crushed.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz connects the dots: “Therefore snares surround you, and sudden peril terrifies you…” Friend, in Eliphaz's mind, Job brought all this on himself.

cards.question: Eliphaz says it is so dark around Job that he cannot see. What else does Eliphaz say covers Job?

cards.text: Now Eliphaz points UP, to God as high as the heavens: “Look at the highest stars, how lofty they are!” Berry, one of my cookie cutter kids, would've pressed his little star face to the window for THIS one.

cards.question: After pointing to how high God is, Eliphaz tells Job what Job supposedly says about Him. True or false: Eliphaz claims Job says thick clouds keep God from seeing us.

cards.text: Eliphaz asks if Job will stay on the ancient path that wicked men have trod. He says those men were snatched away before their time, and their foundations were swept away by a flood.

cards.question: Eliphaz says those wicked men of old were snatched away before their time. What does he say they told God?
True or false: Eliphaz says it was God who filled the houses of those wicked men with good things.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz adds, “…so I stay far from the counsel of the wicked.” He backs away from it like somebody quietly leaving a group chat that just got WAY too heated.

cards.question: Eliphaz says that when the wicked are destroyed, the righteous see it and are ___.

cards.text: Then Eliphaz gives the words of the innocent as they mock: “Surely our foes are destroyed, and fire has consumed their excess.”

After the whole LIST, Eliphaz turns around and hands Job an invitation: “Reconcile now and be at peace with Him; thereby good will come to you.” That's like your boss chewing you out for an hour and then sliding you a cookie.

cards.question: Eliphaz tells Job to receive instruction from God's mouth. Where does Eliphaz say Job should lay up God's words?
True or false: Eliphaz tells Job that if he returns to the Almighty, he will be restored.

cards.text: Eliphaz's next if: Job has to remove injustice from his tents and send his gold to the dust, even the gold of Ophir to the stones of the ravines. Friend, I spent YEARS in the dust at the back of a junk drawer, and nobody EVER sent gold down to keep me company.

cards.question: If Job lets go of his gold, what does Eliphaz say will be his gold and his finest silver?

cards.text: Then, Eliphaz says, Job will delight in the Almighty and lift up his face to God. I think Eliphaz is pitching Job a whole comeback MOVIE, and he's already cutting the trailer.

cards.question: True or false: Eliphaz says that even if Job prays to God, God will stay silent.
Earlier, Eliphaz said it was so dark around Job that he could not see. Now he promises that Job's decisions will be carried out and ___ will shine on his ways.

cards.text: Eliphaz even says, “When men are brought low and you say, ‘Lift them up!’ then He will save the lowly.” Friend, Job just went from the villain of this speech to the guy speaking up for EVERYBODY.

cards.question: Eliphaz ends by saying God will rescue someone through the cleanness of Job's hands. Who does he say God will deliver that way?

answers.text: Even one who is not innocent

cards.text: Grab your apron, friend, because Job's story is FAR from done.
